basics.name: Stefan Strainovic
basics.label: Statistician and Data Scientist
basics.summary: Statistician and Data Scientist with a Master's in Applied Statistics, specializing in building and deploying machine learning models. Experienced in applying ML and deep learning to solve complex problems in both finance (credit risk) and biomedical research (oncology, medical imaging). Passionate about optimization and leveraging data to drive impactful solutions in fast-paced environments.

work.name: Karmen
work.position: Data Scientist & Credit Risk Analyst Intern
work.summary: Developed and deployed machine learning solutions to automate credit risk assessment and internal data processing workflows.
highlights: Researched and built credit risk models (XGBoost, Random Forest), and deployed a scoring UI with Streamlit for the credit team.
Engineered a transaction classification system using TF-IDF to automate the labeling of thousands of financial transactions.
Designed a transaction prioritization algorithm using clustering to optimize the manual labeling process for model training.
Researched a CNN-based approach for identifying bank statements from PDF images to automate document sorting.
Contributed to various internal tools, model monitoring dashboards, and bug fixes.

work.name: Ensicaen (CNRS & Cyceron)
work.summary: Conducted statistical analysis for a joint research project on the effects of radiation therapy on the immune system.
highlights: Analyzed the impact of X-ray and proton brain irradiation on T-lymphocyte sub-types using R.
Developed and interpreted multiple linear regression models to explore correlations between treatment variables and lymphocyte concentrations.
Contributed to a deeper understanding of the immunological effects of radiation therapy.

education.institution: University of Paris 7 Diderot, Paris, France
courses: Core & Applied Mathematics: Gained a strong foundation in key mathematical fields including Algebra, Analysis, Differential Equations, and Optimization.
Computational & Probabilistic Modeling: Developed proficiency in Probability, Statistics, and Numerical Analysis, complemented by skills in programming and algorithms.

Project-Based Learning: Successfully completed multiple mathematical and pre-professional projects, applying theoretical knowledge to practical challenges and enhancing research and problem-solving abilities.
Statistical Theory and Methadology: Rigorous training in multivariate data analysis, classification, regression models, and time series analysis for forecasting and modeling stochastic processes.
Implementation of statistical models and algorithms: Implementation using statistical software (Pythong, R and SAS), with a focus on Operational Research, Discrete Optimization and Machine Learning.
Internships and Projects: Executed internships in statistical research (Oncology) and machine learning (Finance), as well as personal projects in Deep Learning applied to Medical Imaging.

projects.name: Brain Tumor Classification with CNNs
projects.summary: Developed a machine learning model to classify brain tumors from MRI images, achieving 98% accuracy. This project served as a foundational step into deep learning and computer vision.
highlights: Implemented Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification.
Utilized transfer learning with pre-trained models like VGG16 and VGG19.
Applied data augmentation techniques to enhance dataset diversity and prevent overfitting.

projects.name: Hackathon: Bacteriophage Genomics Classification
projects.summary: Participated in a biology-focused hackathon to build a model for classifying bacteriophage genomic sequences.
highlights: Fine-tuned a Large Language Model (LLM) to identify which gene sequences correspond to specific phage components (head, neck, tail).
Collaborated in a team to preprocess genomic data and train the model for high-accuracy classification.

projects.name: Hackathon: Predicting Cognitive Decline in Dementia
projects.summary: Developed an ensemble model to predict cognitive decline by analyzing audio and text data from patients.
highlights: Extracted prosodic features (pitch, tone, pause duration) from audio files.
Built an ensemble model combining a BERT-based LLM for text analysis and an MLP for audio and sentiment data.
The final model classifies patients and can be used to track the progression of dementia over time.
